learning_outcomes.text: Students recognize fundamental structures of the already familiar practice of ethical argumentation and are also aware of the central conflicts of interest in economic arrangements.
Students develop a deeper understanding of the inescapability of value judgments in theory and practice. They know basic approaches for justifying trade-offs.

Students become aware of the fact that professional responsibility exists and that it is not possible to remain neutral on this matter. They can classify competing business ethics approaches and recognize their relevance for their own positioning.
Students can make ethically reflected and well-reasoned decisions in the face of conflicts of interest in professional life.

Students recognize ethically challenging situations in professional life. They can assess when a monological evaluation is no longer appropriate and how, in such cases, the necessary knowledge gain and normative agreement can be achieved by involving other actors.

Students can identify conflicts of interest in professional situations and explain them in a differentiated manner. They can knowledgeably justify the systematic importance of ethical requirements for economic actors and their practical implications.
Students recognize the inevitability of professional responsibility and the inherent demand on professional action (as social action) to be able to comprehensively justify actions.

syllabus_topics: The inescapability of value judgments in theory and practice
Objectives of companies and their legitimacy
Limits of the "Business Case for Business Ethics"
Entrepreneurial success in the service of social development
Artificial intelligence and responsibility: Data-based discrimination
Planned obsolescence ("predetermined breaking points" for sales promotion)
Dealing with employees between profit interest and moral demands
Asbestos, Contergan & Co.: Technology impact assessment, major risks and the precautionary principle
Vision, Mission and Code of Ethics
assessment_rules: The portfolio exam comprises 100 points and consists of two written assignments (APS) and a one-hour exam (K1). A maximum of 30 points can be achieved with each of the two APS, and a maximum of 40 points can be achieved with K1. Alternatively, K2 (at the discretion of the examiner) may be chosen.
